records.name: Eskişehir
records.summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Eskişehir — university city, the most youthful-anonymous interior city; Amnesty's 2024 provincial monitoring records that authorities unlawfully prevented its Pride march, in a city that had previously hosted one of the country's few functioning pride events. National frame: the leaked October 2025 draft would criminalise 'conduct contrary to biological sex' and its promotion (up to 3 years) and restrict gender-affirming care (minimum age 25); a 2025 rights report records hostility as explicit state policy, six violations of the right to life, trans people most affected. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

records.name: Gaziantep
records.summary:
Gaziantep sits fully under the national framework with no documented local divergence in either direction: the leaked October 2025 judicial package would criminalise conduct contrary to biological sex and its promotion (up to three years) and restrict gender-affirming care to age 25 and above, while the 2025 national rights report documents hostility as explicit state policy — presidency-centred targeting, censorship, an organisation closed, six violations of the right to life with trans people most affected, and no official protection statistics at all.

Nothing in the record shows this province offering either special danger beyond, or protection beneath, that national baseline; a visibly trans visitor's exposure is the national one, locally enforced.

records.name: İstanbul
records.summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): İstanbul — the whole scene; the Beyoğlu legacy: the district governor's office ordered trans women's apartments on Bayram Street sealed in March 2024; on 18 July 2025 a residential street was blockaded by police with drones and raids (three detained); on 31 July 2025 around 20 trans women were rounded up for identity checks while street, shopping and in cafés, taken to a police station, names recorded and videos filmed ('this is profiling'). Pride has been banned for a ninth consecutive year — 113 detained on 25 June 2023, 46 detained at the 2024 Acıbadem march with judicial controls and travel bans. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.
